points.description: Identifies that fewer than 10 packets in the queue is the complement of the system being full (exactly N = 10 packets, buffer full), i.e. the answer needs the blocking probability P_B (or directly P(X<10) = sum of state probabilities for 0..9).
States the correct M/M/1/N blocking probability formula with utilization ρ = λ/μ = 9/10 = 0.9 and N = 10: P_B = ((1-ρ)ρ^N)/(1-ρ^(N+1)).
points.partial_credit: Formula correct but ρ not identified as 0.9 (or vice versa), give half.

points.description: Multiplies the 60 s observation time by P(X<10) = 1 - P_B and gives the final answer ≈ 56.95 s (about 57 s).

rubric.notes: Full marks need all four steps stated precisely: complement of the full state, correct M/M/1/N formula with ρ=0.9 and N=10, P_B≈0.0508, and 60×(1−P_B)≈56.95 s. A wrong detail (e.g. using M/M/1 without finite buffer, wrong N, or wrong ρ) cancels that point and usually the later ones. A bare final number or vague statement without the method earns nothing for the steps it skips; summing P(0..9) directly is accepted as an alternative.
